title: Support-sensitive cohomological bound on an excellent strictly local punctured spectrum
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $X$ be a Noetherian excellent strictly henselian local scheme with closed point $x$, on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put $U=X\setminus\{x\}$. Let $F$ be a sheaf of $\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$-modules on the small etale site of $U$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], with geometric stalks as in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Let $s\geq0$ be an integer. Suppose that for every $y\in U$ and every geometric point $\bar y$ above $y$ with $F_{\bar y}\neq0$, the closure $\overline{\{y\}}$ taken in $X$ has Krull dimension at most $s$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then
$$H^p(U,F)=0\qquad\text{for every integer }p\geq2s,$$
where cohomology is the right derived global-sections cohomology of the underlying abelian etale sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. No normality, constructibility of $F$, or finite-type-over-a-field hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Expose XVII, Proposition 3.2.1 (printed p. 268), first assertion, with d=s; the support closure is taken in X, not in U. This result has no Stacks tag in the cited source.

proof.text: Write the local scheme $X$ as $\operatorname{Spec}R$, where $R$ is its Noetherian local ring. The cited finite-dimension lemma gives $\dim R=d$ for an integer $d\geq0$. The spectrum dimension identification in the dimension definition gives $\dim X=d$. Thus the finite-dimensional hypothesis of the strict-local bound is satisfied; this imposes no new hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Tag 00KQ, proposition-dimension and the following fundamental inequality; Tag 00KE, definition-Krull

proof.text: Apply the first assertion of [lem-per-strict-local-etale-dimension-bounds] with $S=X$, its closed point equal to $x$, coefficient exponent $n=1$, its dimension $d=\dim X$ from Step 1, and its support bound $e=s$. The coefficient ring is $\mathbf Z/\ell^1\mathbf Z=\mathbf Z/\ell\mathbf Z$, so the input sheaf is exactly $F$ and the complement is exactly $U$. The hypotheses on excellence, strict henselianity and invertibility are precisely those in the statement. Its support hypothesis uses closures in $S=X$, exactly as ours does. Consequently its conclusion is $H^p(U,F)=0$ for every $p\geq2s$. The cited assertion uses ordinary small etale cohomology, so these are the derived global-sections groups specified here. The later supported-cohomology and integral-generic-point clauses of that node are not needed.
